body:
1. **Compare json_view values without a vector per container and a `basic_json` per number.**
   - Objects are compared in a lockstep walk over the equal text, where the member order matches.
   - A type and array-size pre-check comes first.
   - The member vectors grow geometrically.
2. **Check the float tokens of a json_document image without a sort and a scan of every character.**
   - The tokens are sorted only when they are unsorted.
   - The recorded float shape is checked 8 digits per step.
3. **No per-object allocations when `ordered_json` objects are resolved.**
   - Duplicate keys are resolved in one working vector owned by the comparison, whose capacity is reused. Before, each compared object allocated one vector, or two per side when the key order differs.
   - Objects with unique keys need no working memory at all.

## Numbers

Instructions vs develop (Linux GCC 13 / Clang 18):

| case | change |
|---|---|
| `==` of equal copies, twitter | -49 % / -52 % |
| `==` of equal copies, citm | -90 % / -89 % |
| `==` of equal copies, jeopardy | -85 % |
| `ordered_json` documents | -89 ... -91 % |
| editable documents | -46 ... -88 % |
| view against `json` | -14 ... -66 % |
| `load(image_check::full)` canada | -50 % / -42 % |
| `load(image_check::full)` twitter | -31 % / -35 % |

Commit 3 alone, on top of commits 1–2, in instructions (callgrind, GCC 13 / Clang 18), with timings from the A/B harness on the VPS:

| case | instructions | time |
|---|---|---|
| `ordered_json` view `==` `ordered_json`, twitter | -6.1 % / -5.9 % | -5.2 % |
| `ordered_json`, 20,000 small objects with a duplicate key | -23 ... -26 % | -31 % |
| all other rows (`json`, citm, canada, view `==` view) | -1.2 ... +0.3 % | — |

## Validation

- **Sweep:** one difference placed at about 1,900 positions in 7 documents, for 5 comparison kinds, gives the same results as develop.
  - No placement is slower beyond noise, with one exception: a difference in the first token of an ordered editable document is +3 ... 8 % slower (about 10 ns of 220 ns), with fewer instructions.
- **Fuzzed differential check:** comparison, and image save/load, with corrupted images, equal to develop.
- All json_view unit tests with ASan/UBSan, in C++11 and C++20.
- Commit 3: a new test of `ordered_json` objects with duplicate keys (3 to 40 members, keys in either order, many objects in one comparison) against `ordered_json`; the full suite with ASan/UBSan.
- All commits build on their own, and each commit's `single_include` is a fresh `make amalgamate`.

## Public API

No breaking changes.

Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.

No: the tail check uses `n - 8`, not `i`. It's now in the for-init, here and in `bytes_equal()`, which had the same pattern. (`bytes_less()` keeps it outside, because its second loop continues from `i`.) Fixed in `55cdc93ff`.
